The athlete

Josh Harrison. 1:14 to 1:05 in one season.

Bewdley, Worcestershire. HYROX Pro athlete, coach and creator — building Hybrid Hub between race blocks. Open solo 1:06:13 at ExCeL London, pro solo 1:05:43 in Bologna, a 57:14 pro doubles with Rio Quarry in Manchester. The training blocks, the race weekends and the honest debriefs all go on the channel.

Coming back from a layoff
  1. Drop intensity before volume — keep the sessions, cut the load. The habit is the hard part; the fitness comes back.
  2. Race doubles first. Splitting the stations means you can go hard for 30 seconds and recover — banking confidence instead of a blow-up.
  3. A plan beats guesswork. Ask Josh — that's what the coaching page is for.

HYROX has eight stations. The ninth station — a dinner table full of people who get why your legs are wrecked. No pace requirement, no partner needed, don't even need to have raced. If you're just curious you're the most welcome of all — sit down, eat, hear the stories, leave with a plan.

items.title: HYROX confirms the 26/27 UK calendar
items.summary: London, Glasgow, Cardiff and Birmingham all land on the new season calendar, with the usual sell-out warnings attached. Full dates and venues are on the official site.
items.take: Book the hotel before you book the heat — Saturday waves go first and nobody enjoys a 6 a.m. start in a city an hour away. Bologna taught me that one.

items.title: Doubles fields keep getting quicker
items.summary: Pro doubles times across the season are trending down, with more sub-hour pairs turning up at every major race.
items.take: 57:14 isn't a flex, it's a warning — the pairs game is where this sport is heading. Find your partner before you need one; the race-mate board exists for a reason.
